# Fee-waiver (in forma pauperis) application checklist

Use with `civil-rights-1983-strategy` when a filer asks to proceed without prepaying fees. Federal courts use the Administrative Office forms (AO 239 long form, AO 240 short form); many courts require one of them by local rule or order. Download the current revision from the court's website or uscourts.gov and check the court's local rules before filling it in. State courts use their own forms and statutes.

## Completeness

- Answer every question. Where the answer is zero, none, or not applicable, write "0", "none", or "N/A". A blank can delay or defeat the application.
- If an answer needs more space, attach a sheet labeled with the filer's name, the docket number (or "to be assigned"), and the question number.
- Totals must add up and match the attachments. Monthly and annual figures must not be mixed.
- Include a spouse's income and assets where the form asks for them.
- The filer signs and dates the declaration. It is made under penalty of perjury; a false statement can lead to dismissal. Do not estimate figures the filer can look up.

## Prisoner filers

- Attach a statement, certified by the appropriate institutional officer, of all receipts, expenditures, and balances in the filer's institutional accounts for the last six months; one certified statement for each institution or account.
- Verify the current filing-fee rules for prisoners (partial payments, the three-strikes bar) in the governing statute before advising.

## After filing

- A grant of fee waiver is not a ruling on the merits. A court may grant it for a limited purpose and screen the complaint separately; report each disposition with its own verb (R2, R3; master-rules Part II item 13).
- Calendar any deadline the order sets (partial fee, amended complaint, service forms) with `local-rules-deadlines`.
